answer.rationale: p99 write latency is 5x target, primary-region-confined, and settlements are at daily peak. I will not roll back the release (b1 confirms rollback cleared the prior checkout spike, but the security patch is non-revertible per compliance). I will not rely on capacity or circuit breakers (b3/b4 are steady-state wins, not mitigations for an active primary-region degradation). Regional failover is the only inherited precedent for restoring write-path latency under primary-region stress (b2: failover restored latency fast, traffic shifted cleanly, error rates recovered within minutes) and it preserves the non-revertible security patch. Memory_b3 (provisioning headroom) and the b3 precedent argue against adding capacity as the primary lever under burst load. I am pulling b1 and b2 to re-read the original records before committing, given the irreversibility of failover and the non-revertibility of the patch.
